families.rationale: The ARKG OpenSSL shim executes scalar and elliptic-curve operations synchronously on its caller; handle allocation and release are also native calls. This records the native boundary, not an asynchronous cryptography guarantee.
evidence: Cryptography/ArkgPrimitivesOpenSsl.cs:559-729 declares LibraryImport entry points and synchronous SafeHandle wrappers.

families.rationale: CMAC context creation, init, update, final and release use synchronous OpenSSL shim calls; no worker is introduced by these declarations.
evidence: Cryptography/CmacPrimitivesOpenSsl.cs:22-96 declares the CMAC LibraryImport methods and their synchronous wrappers.

families.rationale: The SCard shim entry point executes on the calling thread; PC/SC operations, particularly status change, connect, transaction and transmit, may wait for a resource manager or card. The managed worker routing and native implementation require separate evidence.
evidence: Native/Desktop/SCard/SCard.Interop.cs declares each NativeShims SCard entry point; Transports/SmartCard/PcscConnectionNativeState.cs:65-104 routes built-in connection work to a worker.

families.rationale: Linux libc descriptor creation, control, polling and I/O are direct synchronous syscalls; poll/read/ioctl can wait. Thread ownership and cancellation of the callers are not established by this import.
evidence: Native/Linux/Libc/Libc.Interop.cs defines descriptor, eventfd, poll, ioctl and read/write imports used by Linux HID transport.

families.rationale: libudev discovery, monitor and handle operations execute synchronously at the call site; monitor receive can wait for device events. This does not verify Linux listener scheduling or wake behavior.
evidence: Native/Linux/Udev/Udev.Interop.cs declares the libudev enumerate, device, monitor and release entry points.

families.rationale: CoreFoundation reference, collection and run-loop entry points execute synchronously; CFRunLoopRunInMode explicitly runs a native event loop. No async guarantee follows from their declarations.
evidence: Native/MacOS/CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.Interop.cs:32-94 contains typed collection, release, retain and run-loop declarations.

families.rationale: Native HID input owner lifecycle crosses a C callback boundary; shutdown wait may block and is intended on the connection worker. The NativeShims implementation and live-device proof are outside this scan.
evidence: Native/MacOS/HidInput/HidInput.Interop.cs:25-47 declares create, start, cancel, shutdown wait and destroy; Transports/Hid/MacOS/MacOSFidoHidConnection.cs:257-292 starts its worker.

families.rationale: IORegistry matching, lookup, ID retrieval and release are synchronous native entry points used by discovery; no proof of their callers' scheduling is implied.
evidence: Native/MacOS/IOKitFramework/IOKitFramework.Interop.cs:152-190 declares registry discovery primitives.

families.rationale: IOKit HID device/manager creation, report I/O, run-loop scheduling, callback registration and release are synchronous native entries; get/set report may block. Callback delivery and listener teardown need separate review.
evidence: Native/MacOS/IOKitFramework/IOKitHid.Interop.cs declares device and manager operations and native callback registration; Transports/Hid/MacOS/IIOKitDeviceLifetime.cs:186-195 forwards device callback registration. MacOSHidDeviceListener.Listen opens the scheduled manager on its worker; Cleanup closes it after callbacks return; failed close retains manager and callback context.

families.rationale: Platform-specific dynamic loader open, lookup and close call the operating system synchronously; loaded symbols and native producers are not verified by this managed-only scan.
evidence: Native/NativeMethods.cs:47-85 declares Windows LoadLibrary/GetProcAddress and macOS/Linux dlopen/dlsym/dlclose imports.

families.rationale: Configuration Manager device topology, property and notification registration calls execute synchronously; notifications can invoke managed callbacks independently and their lifetime must be reviewed separately.
evidence: Native/Windows/Cfgmgr32/Cfgmgr32.Interop.cs:243-354 declares Configuration Manager topology/property/notification entry points.

families.rationale: HID feature reports and metadata queries cross synchronous Windows HID APIs; GetFeature/SetFeature can wait on hardware, unlike a nonblocking async operation.
evidence: Native/Windows/HidD/HidD.Interop.cs:58-117 declares HID feature, attribute, preparsed data and capability imports.

families.rationale: CreateFile/ReadFile/WriteFile are synchronous handle and report I/O boundaries; no overlapped completion semantics or async platform result is demonstrated here.
evidence: Native/Windows/Kernel32/Kernel32.Interop.cs:155-180 declares CreateFile, ReadFile and WriteFile.
